correctness.rationale: The left-coset formula is exact; the unitary F_p Fourier transform gives p independent q-column blocks. At frequency zero the P measurements have full rank q and the complements alone rank one when present. All nonzero frequencies are rectangular minors of the prime Fourier matrix, rank min(m,q), by the fully reconstructed cyclotomic-integer proof. This yields the exact kernel formula, normal spectral blocks, Cauchy–Binet determinants and full-affine three-level eigenvalues. The independent integer-incidence checker passed 610 exact modular-rank tests and 22 complex spectral tests; no finite computation substitutes for the all-parameter proof.

value.rationale: The natural problem is choosing the smallest number of complete cyclic-coset measurement directions on a finite nonabelian affine group. The result classifies every subfamily (including exact nullities), proves all minimal choices succeed with only q extra measured scalars, and determines their normal determinant and the complete three-level full-affine stability spectrum. This is a structurally motivated infinite-family reconstruction theorem, not just code, known-table recomputation, or arbitrary finite slicing.
